To apply the ratio test we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{x}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)^{n+2}{3}^{n+1}{x}^{n+1}}{(n+1)^{3/2}}\cdot \frac{{n}^{3/2}}{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{-3x{n}^{3/2}}{(n+1)^{3/2}}| \\  & =3|-x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{3/2} \\  & =3|x|\cdot 1 \\  & =3|x|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for $|x|<\frac{1}{3}.$ So, the radius of convergence is $\frac{1}{3},$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x|=\frac{1}{3},$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=-\frac{1}{3}$ and $x=\frac{1}{3}$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=\frac{1}{3}$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{x}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{(\frac{3}{3})}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}+\frac{1}{{3}^{3/2}}-\frac{1}{{4}^{3/2}}+⋯\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the alternating series test.   So the endpoint $x=\frac{1}{3}$ is included in our interval.

- When $x=-\frac{1}{3}$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{x}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(-1)^{n}{(\frac{3}{3})}^{n}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{2n+1}}{{n}^{3/2}} \\  & =-(1+\frac{1}{{2}^{3/2}}+\frac{1}{{3}^{3/2}}+\frac{1}{{4}^{3/2}}+⋯)\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the $p$-series test.   So the endpoint $x=-\frac{1}{3}$ is included in our interval.

Therefore, the interval of convergence is $[-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}].$
